facts.text: Appleton was named after Samuel Appleton, a New England philanthropist who donated $10,000 to a college library, though he never visited Wisconsin.
Lawrence University, founded in 1847, was one of the first co‑educational institutions in the nation and still sits in Appleton.
The Vulcan Street Plant, the nation’s first hydro‑electric central station, began operating on September 30, 1882, powering Appleton’s paper mills.
Appleton’s history includes a 1877 telephone built by Alfred Galpin, connecting his bank to his home long before commercial phones.
The Appleton Historical Society hosts a Riverside Cemetery Walk each August, guiding visitors through graves of the city’s founders and builders.
Appleton’s downtown features the Scheig Center Gardens, a public botanical garden that once hosted the Gardens of the Fox Cities and now showcases seasonal plants.
